prompt: A repeating tone rises in frequency while its amplitude stays the same. What happens to its period?

options.explanation: Correct. More cycles must fit into each second, so each cycle takes less time.
A longer cycle means fewer repetitions per second and a lower frequency.
Period and frequency describe the same repetition timing; changing one changes the other.
Period measures time; wavelength measures distance in a medium.

workedExample: Frequency measures cycles per second. A higher count needs shorter cycles. Amplitude controls the size of the swing, so keeping it unchanged does not prevent the timing change.
